1441:
(a) Unlawful waste placement. It shall be unlawful for any person to place, deposit or permit to be deposited in any unsanitary manner on public or private property within the county or in any area under the jurisdiction of the county or the authority, any human or animal excrement, garbage, or other objectionable waste. It shall be unlawful to discharge to any natural outlet within the county, or in any area under the jurisdiction of the county or the authority, any sewage or other polluted waters, except where suitable treatment has been provided in accordance with this division. Except as hereinafter provided, it shall be unlawful to construct or maintain any privy, privy vault, septic tank, cesspool or other facility intended or used for the disposal of sewage.
(b) Connection to public systems. In the interest of the public health, sanitation and general welfare, all buildings and structures located within the authority's service delivery area, of every nature, use and design, intended for human occupancy, employment, recreation, or for other purposes shall have a proper source of potable drinking water and sewage disposal. The owner of each house, building, or property used for human occupancy, employment, recreation, or for other purposes is hereby required at the owner's expense to install suitable toilet facilities therein, and to connect the facilities directly into the authority's wastewater system in accordance with the authority's regulations, if such connection is required by state law, to wit, the state's manual for on-site sewage management systems, section 290-5-26-.03 (Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. 290-5-26-.03), which requires connection to public sewer when it is located within 200 feet of the owner's property or is located in a public right-of-way, road, or alley abutting the property.
(c) No permit issuance. No permit for the construction of any residence, building or other facility which cannot be served by public sanitary sewer shall be issued, and no certificate for the use and occupancy for any existing residence, building or other facility which cannot be served by public sanitary sewer shall be issued, unless a septic tank or individual sewage management system permit has been issued by the board of health in conformity with any state-wide minimum standards for on-site sewage management systems and the regulations of the county board of health then in force and effect.
(d) Connection upon failed system. Upon the failure of a septic tank or individual sewage management system, use of such system shall be discontinued. The property owner shall cause the building or structure to be connected to the public sanitary sewer system if such connection is required by state law, to wit, the state's manual for on-site sewage management systems, section 290-5-26-.03 (Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. 290-5-26-.03), which requires connection to public sewer when it is located within 200 feet of the owner's property or is located in a public right-of-way, road, or alley abutting the property. Abandoned septic tanks and individual systems shall either be removed by the owner or filled with suitable material so as not to constitute a hazard or nuisance.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. I(4), 9-15-2005)
1442:
A separate building sewer shall be provided for every building and structure intended for human occupancy and accessible to the public sanitary sewer system, unless for good cause shown the director issues a written permit to allow more than one building or structure to be connected on a common building sewer.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. I(5), 9-15-2005)
1443:
Unless otherwise provided, the volume of wastewater delivered to the authority's wastewater system will be based upon the quantity of water purchased from, and metered by, the authority. If the volume of water delivered to the authority's wastewater system is greater or less than the volume purchased from the authority, the user shall make known to the authority such differences. If differences do exist, it shall be the obligation of the user to install authority-approved meters or other devices to determine the portion or quantity of wastewater delivered to the authority's wastewater system. At locations readily accessible for meter reading by the authority, separate water meters installed in the county right-of-way are preferred for measuring nonsewered consumptive water usage. The authority may consider establishing a constant ratio, factor or percentage to be applied to the metered water quantity delivered by the water system in order to determine the waste delivered by the user. Determining, as well as justifying, the factor to the authority will be the responsibility of the user. The value of this factor may be periodically reviewed for accuracy by the authority. Other methods may be established by the authority to estimate the quantity of wastewater released to the sanitary sewer which considers the amount of water consumed during different seasons. Users which claim wastewater volumes to be inaccurately determined by these methods shall bear the expense of installing authority-approved meters to estimate flows to the authority's wastewater system more accurately.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. I(6), 9-15-2005)
1445:
(a) Generally. All extensions of the authority's wastewater system shall be designed and built in accordance with standards adopted by the authority. No installation of pipe or other materials for sewer extensions shall be allowed until the required information is received and the design is approved by the director. Inspection and acceptance procedures shall be specified in the standards adopted by the authority.
(b) Prohibitions. No building sewers shall be connected to a sanitary sewer until as-built drawings are received and until the extension has been inspected, tested, and accepted in writing for county operation and maintenance. Groundwater, rainwater, mud, and gravel shall be kept out of the sanitary sewer system at all times, including during construction.
(c) Other regulations. Design and construction of a sanitary sewer extension shall comply with all local, state, and federal rules and regulations pertaining to sewer installation, including but not limited to rules and regulations for safety, erosion and sediment control, stream buffer protection, wetlands, and water quality standards.
(d) Authority. The authority is hereby authorized to issue and from time to time amend the standards of construction referenced in this section. Any such standards of construction shall be available to the public at the offices of the authority.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. I(8), 9-15-2005)
1446:
(a) Generally. All persons owning or operating septage pump trucks or other liquid waste transport trucks shall not discharge, directly or indirectly, wastewater into the authority's wastewater system, unless such person shall first have applied for and received a mobile discharge operation ("MDO") permit from the authority. Each hauler is required to comply with any and all rules and regulations adopted by the authority for haulers. Persons doing business under a MDO permit shall not discharge into the county any sewage which originated outside of the boundaries of the county. Anyone found guilty of discharging into the county such "holding tank" waste known to have originated outside of the county shall be subject to a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 for each violation.
(b) Permit. The MDO permit shall have a one-time nonrefundable fee as may be established by the authority, provided that such permit shall be subject to revocation by the authority for violation of any provision of this article or reasonable regulation established by the authority. Such permits shall be limited to the discharge of wastewater which has none of the prohibited substances enumerated in division 2 of this article. The owners of such vehicles shall affix and display the permit number on the side of each vehicle used for such purposes.
(c) Discharge locations and conditions. The director shall designate the locations and times where such trucks may be discharged, and may refuse to accept any truckload of waste where it appears to the authority that the waste could interfere with the effective operation of the authority's wastewater system. Further, it shall be the responsibility of the dumping vehicle operator to advise the treatment plant operator of the contents of his load and its source prior to dumping. The director may collect samples of each hauled load to ensure compliance with applicable standards. Anyone found guilty of discharging into the authority's wastewater system at a location not approved for dumping shall be subject to a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 for each incident.
(d) No hauled industrial waste will be accepted without express permission from the director. The director shall require haulers of industrial waste to obtain wastewater discharge permits in accordance with the application and approval provisions set forth in sections 54-40 through 54-42. The director also may prohibit the disposal of hauled industrial waste. The discharge of hauled industrial waste is subject to all other requirements of this article.
(e) Waste-tracking form. All industrial waste haulers must submit to the authority a waste-tracking form for every load. This form shall include, at a minimum, the name and address of the industrial waste hauler, permit number, truck identification, names and addresses of sources of waste, and volume and characteristics of waste. The form shall identify the type of industry and known or suspected waste constituents. In any event, no industrial waste hauler shall be permitted to haul and discharge hazardous wastes (as identified by the May 19, 1980 Environmental Protection Agency Hazardous Waste Regulations, part 261 or any revision thereof or the Georgia Comprehensive Waste Management Act and associated rules) into the authority's wastewater system.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. I(9), 9-15-2005)
1449:

1453:
No user shall ever increase the use of process water or, in any way, attempt to dilute a discharge as a partial or complete substitute for adequate treatment to achieve compliance with the limitations contained in the federal pretreatment standards, or in any other pollutant specific limitation developed by this article and EPD. The director may impose mass limitations on users who are using dilution to meet applicable pretreatment standards or requirements or in other cases when the imposition of mass limitations is appropriate. (Res. No. 2005-55, art. II(7), 9-15-2005)
1456:
(a) General prohibition. There shall be no discharge of grease trap waste into the authority's wastewater system, unless a license is issued by the director for good cause shown.
(b) Requirements.
(1) Preparation of food for retail or commercial purposes. All users involved in the preparation of food for retail or commercial purposes shall provide oil/grease interceptors or traps. Additionally, any user who generates a wastewater which contains greater than the quantity of oil and grease regulated under section 54-70, and provided that the excess oil and grease is floatable and can be effectively removed in an oil/grease interceptor or trap, then said user will be required to install a grease/oil interceptor.
(2) Unusually large quantities or grit. All users whose wastewater stream is associated with unusually large quantities or grit, sand or gravel shall be required to install, operate, and maintain a sand/grit trap. All car/truck wash systems and poultry hatcheries shall be required to install a sand/grit trap. Their design and installation shall be approved by the authority.
(3) Applicability. The requirements of this subsection shall not apply to private living quarters or dwelling units.
(c) Design criteria.
(1) For restaurants and other eating establishments. All sand and oil/grease interceptors used in conjunction with restaurants or other eating establishments shall have a capacity of 15 gallons per seat, except that no grease trap shall be smaller than 750 gallons or larger than 3,000 gallons.
(2) For facilities other than eating establishments. All sand and oil/grease interceptors used in conjunction with facilities other than eating establishments shall have a capacity that will provide not less than ten minutes nor more than 30 minutes retention time at the peak eight hour flowrate; flowthrough velocities shall not exceed one foot per second at the peak eight hour flowrate.
(3) Accordance to state minimum standards. Where such parameters have not been otherwise set forth herein, all sand and oil/grease interceptors shall be sized, located and constructed in accordance with the provisions of the state minimum standards plumbing code adopted by the water and sewerage authority in conjunction with the state Uniform Codes Act.
(d) Maintenance.
(1) By user. All grease, oil and sand/grit interceptors or traps shall be maintained by the user at their expense, in continuously efficient operation at all times.
(2) Proper removal and disposal. In the maintaining of these interceptors, the owner shall be responsible for the proper removal and disposal by appropriate means of the captured material, and shall maintain records of the dates, and means of disposal, which are subject to review by the director. The frequency of removal shall be such as to ensure that no overflows of oil, grease, or sand, or other grit material into the wastewater system ever results.
(3) Records. Material haulers are required to give a manifest to the producer each time materials are removed. As materials are removed, the manifest from the haulers are required to be sent to the director within 30 days of their removal.
(4) Fees. The authority will inspect interceptors yearly at a fee as set forth in the county fee schedule in section 18-19. If a reinspection is required an additional charge will be given as set forth in the county fee schedule.
(e) Proper disposal of collected materials. Any removal and hauling of the collected materials not performed by the owner's employees must be performed by currently licensed waste disposal firms. All material shall be disposed of at a facility permitted to receive such waste. Under no circumstances shall the collected materials ever be returned to the wastewater system.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. II(8), 9-15-2005)
1459:
(a) Generally. All nondomestic users (who are not determined to be significant industrial users) must have issued to them a general permit prior to connection to the authority's wastewater system. Any violation of the terms and conditions of a permit shall be deemed a violation of this division and subject the user to the sanctions set forth in this article. Obtaining a permit does not relieve a user of its obligation to comply with all federal and state pretreatment standards or regulations. Prior or subsequent to the issuance of a permit, the user is required to submit to the authority revised plans whenever alterations or additions to the user's premises or operations vary from the original submitted application. The director may also initiate inquiries concerning revisions and process changes at six-month intervals.
(b) Application process. All nondomestic users shall complete and submit to the director a sanitary sewer discharge permit application, together with any applicable application fee. Proposed new users shall make application no later than 90 days prior to their intended date of connection to the authority's wastewater system. The sanitary sewer discharge permit application shall be on a form provided by the director and shall be used for the purposes of determining whether the industry is a "significant industrial user," issuing a permit, and for other purposes. The sanitary sewer discharge permit application (which shall be the only permit application required for nondomestic users and those ultimately determined to be significant industrial users) shall include the following information, at a minimum:
(1) Name, address and location, if different from the address.
(2) SIC number according to the Standard Industrial Classification Manual, U.S. Office of Management and Budget, 1987, as amended.
(3) Wastewater constituents and characteristics.
(4) Time and duration of contribution.
(5) Average daily and peak wastewater flow rates, including daily, monthly and seasonal variations if any.
(6) Site plans, floor plans, mechanical and plumbing plans and details to show all sewers, sewer connections and appurtenances by size, location and elevation.
(7) Description of activities, facilities and plant processes on the premises, including all materials, which are or could be discharged.
(8) Each product produced by type, amount, process and rate of production.
(9) Type and amount of raw materials processed (average and maximum per day).
(10) Number and type of employees and hours of operation of plant and proposed or actual hours of operation of pretreatment system.
(11) Any other information as may be deemed by the authority to be necessary to evaluate the permit application.
(12) All wastewater discharge permit applications and user reports must be signed by the user or an authorized representative of the user and contain the following certification statement (which requirement is hereinafter referred to in this section as the certification):
"I certify under penalty of law that this document and all attachments were prepared under my direction or supervision in accordance with a system designed to ensure that qualified personnel properly gather and evaluate the information submitted. Based on my inquiry of the person or persons who manage the system, or those persons directly responsible for gathering the information, the information submitted is, to the best of my knowledge and belief, true, accurate, and complete. I am aware that there are significant penalties for submitting false information, including the possibility of fine and imprisonment for knowing violations."
(c) Review and determination. The director will evaluate the data furnished by the user and may require additional information. Upon completion of the evaluation, the director shall issue or deny a general permit within 45 calendar days of receipt of the application. The director may deny an application, in writing, stating the reasons for the denial. If the director determines that the applicant is a significant industrial user, the director shall notify the applicant of the requirement to be considered for the issuance of a significant industrial user permit within 45 calendar days of receipt of the original application.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. III(1), 9-15-2005)
1460:
(a) Generally. All significant industrial users, as that term is defined in section 54-40, proposing to connect to the authority's wastewater system must obtain a permit ("SIU permit") before connecting to the authority's system. Any violation of the terms and conditions of a permit shall be deemed a violation of this article and subject the user to the sanctions set forth in this article. Obtaining a permit does not relieve a user of its obligation to comply with all federal and state pretreatment standards or regulations. Prior or subsequent to the issuance of a permit, the user is required to submit to the authority revised plans whenever alterations or additions to the user's premises or operations vary from the original submitted application. The director may also initiate inquiries concerning revisions and process changes at six-month intervals.
(b) Application process. All significant industrial users shall complete and file with the director an application for a permit consistent with the requirements for the application set forth in section 54-98(b), accompanied by any applicable application fee. Proposed new users shall make application not less than 90 days prior to their intended date of connection to the authority's wastewater system. The completed permit application for a general permit described in section 54-41 will serve as an application for a SIU permit.
(c) Review and determination. The director will evaluate the data furnished by the user and may require additional information. Within 60 days of receipt of a complete SIU permit application, the director will determine whether or not to issue a SIU permit. The director may deny any application for a SIU permit, in writing, stating the reasons for denial.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. III(2), 9-15-2005)
1461:
All significant industrial users shall comply with the following, in addition to any permit requirements:
(1) Sampling manhole. In order to provide for accurate sampling and measurement of industrial wastes, each significant industrial user shall provide and maintain, on each of its industrial waste outlet sewers, a monitoring station to be located outside the plant. If inside the plant fence, there shall be a gate near the sampling manhole with a key furnished to the authority. There shall be ample room provided in each monitoring station to enable convenient inspection and sampling by the authority or its agent. Also, a parshal flume or other approved flow measurement element and a 110-volt electrical outlet may be required to allow for composite sampling. In certain monitoring stations where noxious fumes may accumulate, the authority may require a fume exhaust system to protect the life and health of the authority employees who are required to enter the monitoring station. The fume exhaust system should extract the fumes from the bottom of the station and provide not less than one air change per minute.
(2) Significant industrial user permit required. It shall be unlawful for any significant industrial user to fail to obtain a significant industrial user ("SIU") permit (as detailed in this section prior to connection to the authority's wastewater system.
(Res. No. 2005-55, art. III(3), 9-15-2005)
